# XY13: 螺蛳牌楼 Luosi Pailou, "East Gate to Hsien Fa Hill"

3D: `/reconstruction/3d.html?b=XY13` · Page: `/xiyanglou#XY13` · Row: `research/buildings/XY13-luosi-pailou/`

## What it was

The east gate of 线法山: three arches, with the side passages leading through side rooms, and vine ornament carved even over the faces of the pillars (S02 p.159). Plate 19 looks east through it to the water and painted hills beyond. The width is not settled: 22.9 m on the plate, 34-49 m for what the plan draws, with no other check (Q16).

## After 1860

It stands in Moore's photograph of the 1870s-80s (S838 Fig.6). Ohlmer and Child did not photograph it. Its later fate was not found.

## Notes

<!-- Yours: regeneration never touches this part. -->

Round 30: a detailed model built from plate 19 (`models/XY13-luosi-pailou/README.md`), 41 points, 0.19 m rms. Readings at 1.3-2.2x on the dossier's frontage of 22.9 m: the arch 2.82 m wide to 5.77 m, the doors 1.25 x 3.55 m, the cornice wavy (6.9 m over the outer columns, 6.6 m over the inner, 7.36 m on the axis), the attic 3.7 m wide to 8.5 m, the trophy group 10.7 m, the towers' urns 12.0 m. The kit's default gate hall GB39 on the wall gap 20 m west, in plate 19's line of sight, is hidden. The size still rests on the dossier's weak module (Q73): Moore's photograph (P0225) is the best hope.
